def round_and_sum(numbers):
    # Round every number in the list to the nearest integer (default behavior of Python's round)
    rounded_numbers = [round(num) for num in numbers]
    
    # Calculate the sum of the rounded numbers
    total_sum = sum(rounded_numbers)
    
    # Multiply by the length of the original list
    result = total_sum * len(numbers)
    
    return result

# Test case verification
if __name__ == "__main__":
    assert round_and_sum([22.4, 4.0, -16.22, -9.10, 11.00, -12.22, 14.20, -5.20, 17.50]) == 243
print("Test passed!")

# Optional: Print the result for verification
result = round_and_sum([22.4, 4.0, -16.22, -9.10, 11.00, -12.22, 14.20, -5.20, 17.50])
print(f"Result: {result}")
